stem.en: A city government builds a stadium on a public park. The construction money would have been spent on the stadium regardless of location. What is the opportunity cost of building it on the park site?

text.en: The park, with its green space and shade.
Nothing, because the construction budget was already committed.
The stadium itself, since that is what was chosen.
Only whatever admission fee the park used to charge visitors.

explanation.en: Opportunity cost is the value of the next-best option given up. The money was going to be spent either way (b mistakes accounting cost for opportunity cost), the chosen option can't be its own cost (c), and a public park's value is far more than any fee it might collect (d). What the city truly gave up by picking this site is the park itself.

hints.en: Ask what existed at that site before, and what the city lost by replacing it.
